learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the basis for the interpretation and description of the problems typical of Hydraulics and Fluid Mechanics.
Identify, formulate and solve the problems of Hydraulics.
Acquire capabilities of design and critical analysis for the problems typical of Hydraulics, also of great complexity.
Solve applicative Hydraulics problems, with specific reference to problems of hydrostatics and hydrodynamics.
Introduce the fundamental laws of Fluid Mechanics, emphasizing the investigation methodologies and the descriptive rigour of the phenomena under scrutiny.
Provide and deepen the theoretical foundations of Continuum Mechanics, with reference to the fluids.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the “scheme of fluid continuum”
The forces acting on a fluid
Quiescent fluids and the equation of the hydrostatic
The pressure in a quiescent fluid
The static thrust of a fluid on planar/non-planar surfaces
The fluids in motion: kinematics and local flow analysis
The principles of fluid mechanics and hydraulics
Thermo-conductive, viscous fluids: constitutive laws and the theorem of mechanical power
The flow problem: the Navier-Stokes equation
Fundamental solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations
Vorticity dynamics and the Bernoulli theorem
The separation of the boundary layer
Problems of design and control of hydraulic plants
Free-surface streams: the steady-uniform flow, the equation for the free-surface location, free-surface solutions for the riverine and torrent regimes
assessment_rules: To access the oral exam, students must pass a written test with a valuation of at least 18/30. The final mark, in thirties, is the sum of the written test mark and an adjustment of -5/30 to +5/30 based on the oral assessment. Honours are awarded for exceptionally clear and full knowledge of topics.
